subject: gk
question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?

options.text: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building
Social mobilisation, economic development, and education

solution:
The correct answer is __**Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Social mobilisation** refers to the process of bringing together all societal sectors to raise awareness, demand, and participation for the empowerment and development of Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
 
• **Capital formation** involves the accumulation of assets and investments to generate income and enhance the financial stability of SHGs.
 
• **Capacity building** focuses on enhancing the skills, knowledge, and abilities of SHG members to improve their organizational and operational efficiency.
 
• These three components together aim to strengthen SHGs, enabling them to become self-reliant and sustainable in their economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**:

 
 
• SHGs are small, economically homogeneous affinity groups of rural poor, coming together to save and mutually contribute to a common fund.
 
• They provide members with support and resources to improve their living standards and economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance**:
 
 
• It is a financial service for low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.
 
• Microfinance includes loans, savings, insurance, and fund transfers to help the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**:
 
 
• It is the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit for vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.
 
• Financial inclusion aims to connect people to the formal banking system to promote economic growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Livelihood Promotion**:
 
 
• It involves creating and enhancing opportunities for the poor to improve their income and employment prospects.
 
• Livelihood promotion includes training, skill development, and access to markets and financial services.
